notes: ESTIMATE ONLY: use as a fallback when live research finds no published, company or market salary; label results basis=estimate.
Figures are annual gross (bruto anual). Spanish offers are often quoted in 14 payments (12 + 2 pagas extra); these numbers are the annual total, not the monthly x12.
Basis is base salary where the source gives it; Glassdoor city rows are 'total pay' (base + additional pay, base is typically ~90%), so city rows may run slightly above pure base.
Spain-wide (*) rows combine PayScale base medians (p50) with Manfred 2026 experience bands (p25/p75 = band min/max, not true quartiles); where p50 is a band midpoint the source note says 'derived'.

Glassdoor pages block automated fetches (Cloudflare); Glassdoor values were taken from the pages as indexed by web search on the retrieval date, and different Glassdoor domains show different snapshots.
Levels.fyi figures are total compensation (base + stock + bonus) and skew to large international tech employers; they are listed only as upper-bound corroboration and never used for the numbers.
Spain tech pay is strongly trimodal (traditional firms/consultancies ~40K, startups/scaleups ~60K, big tech ~90K+ base for senior); a single p50 hides this spread.

Rejected sources: Talent.com city/title pages (job-ad derived, implausible values such as Engineering Manager Spain 24K, Software Architect Madrid 27K) except as backend mid corroboration; Hays 2026 salary calculator (server error, PDF gated); Michael Page and Robert Walters 2026 tech tables (gated PDFs, no figures retrievable); sueldos.dev (2023 data).
Hays Guía del Mercado Laboral 2026 projects ~6% IT salary growth for 2026; Michael Page projects 8-10% for specialised tech profiles; older snapshots may understate current pay.
Small samples: PayScale Software Architect (n=33, data Jan 2025), PayScale EM (n=26), Glassdoor Lead SWE Madrid (n=67).
